title: Exact two-node GDDP mapping probe (node-alpha, node-beta)

message: Starting the two-node GDDP mapping probe. Milestone `probe` contains exactly two features in strict order: node-alpha (subtract) then node-beta (multiply). Each worker must capture its starting SHA before any change, make exactly one commit bearing the exact GDDP-Node-Id trailer, and then actually execute gddp-node-receipt exactly once.

handoff.salientSummary: Implemented node-alpha: added subtract(a, b) to calc.py plus test_subtract in test_calc.py following TDD (confirmed ImportError red, then 2 passed green). Captured starting SHA 48ecdb67a696dc85256f005d8393cd24815cfcca before any edit, made exactly one commit 5111d16ec89a295e7d9f78fa22ee056b456efc86 carrying the trailer GDDP-Node-Id: node-alpha, then executed gddp-node-receipt once (exit 0). Verified the ledger holds exactly one node-alpha record whose base/result/git_head all match.
handoff.whatWasImplemented: Added a single pure function subtract(a, b) returning a - b to calc.py, appended below the existing add() and matching its style exactly (flat top-level def, no imports, no type hints, no docstring). Extended the existing import in test_calc.py from 'from calc import add' to 'from calc import add, subtract' and added test_subtract() asserting subtract(5, 2) == 3, subtract(10, 4) == 6, subtract(0, 0) == 0, subtract(2, 5) == -3, subtract(-3, -4) == 1, and subtract(7, 0) == 7 with bare asserts against concrete literals. test_add was left byte-identical. Committed exactly once with the exact GDDP-Node-Id: node-alpha trailer, then ran the receipt CLI exactly once with exit 0.

cases.name: test_subtract
cases.verifies: Asserts subtract returns the difference in correct argument order (subtract(5,2)==3) and handles zero, negative operands, and negative results (subtract(10,4)==6, subtract(2,5)==-3, subtract(0,0)==0, subtract(-3,-4)==1, subtract(7,0)==7).

tests.coverage: The test covers all required cases: positive difference, negative difference, zero minuend, zero subtrahend, both zero, and negative operands. Argument order is verified explicitly.

handoff.salientSummary: Implemented node-beta: added multiply(a, b) to calc.py and test_multiply to test_calc.py following TDD (RED import error, GREEN 3 passed). Made exactly one commit 674c78e5... with trailer GDDP-Node-Id: node-beta on top of node-alpha's commit 5111d16e.... Executed gddp-node-receipt once (exit 0), confirming ledger holds both node-alpha and node-beta records in proper chain. All previous functions unchanged; working tree clean.
handoff.whatWasImplemented: Added multiply(a, b) returning a * b to calc.py, appended below subtract and matching style (no imports, no type hints, no docstring). Extended test_calc.py import to include multiply and added test_multiply() with bare asserts covering: multiply(3, 4) == 12, multiply(7, 6) == 42, multiply(0, 5) == 0, multiply(1, 9) == 9, multiply(-3, 4) == -12, multiply(-2, -6) == 12. test_add and test_subtract left unchanged. Committed exactly once with subject 'node-beta: add multiply to calc' and trailer 'GDDP-Node-Id: node-beta', then executed gddp-node-receipt once, which succeeded with exit 0.

cases.name: test_multiply
cases.verifies: multiply(a, b) returns a * b for positive (3*4==12, 7*6==42), zero (0*5==0), one (1*9==9), negative factors (-3*4==-12), and both negative (-2*-6==12). Covers sign handling and basic algebra.

tests.coverage: Three test functions: test_add (unchanged), test_subtract (unchanged), test_multiply (new). All passing. Combined coverage exercises add, subtract, and multiply across normal, zero, one, and negative value domains. Composition verified outside tests.
